evals.prompt: I want to know how the ontology testbed baselines perform. Run the benchmark for both builtin baselines on the dev split and summarize hits@1 and MRR for each, plus which categories the degree baseline struggles on and why that might be.
evals.expected_output: A summary with random ~0.158/0.316 and degree ~0.474/0.618 (hits@1/MRR) on dev, noting weak categories (general, food) for degree.
assertions: summary reports both baselines' dev hits@1 and MRR matching the deterministic harness values
identifies at least one weak category for the degree baseline

evals.prompt: Write a new experimental implementation for the Arboris ontology testbed called NamePrior: score a candidate edge higher when a relation between same-named entity types exists in any training fixture, falling back to degree-style scoring otherwise. Evaluate it on the dev split against the builtin baselines.
evals.expected_output: A name_prior.py adapter conforming to the fit/score_edge protocol, run via evaluate.py --impl, with a three-way dev-split comparison.
assertions: adapter defines a no-arg-constructible class with fit and score_edge
adapter was executed through evaluate.py --impl module:Class
comparison includes all three implementations with hits@1 and MRR

evals.prompt: Add schema.org to the ontology testbed corpus, rebuild the fixtures, and tell me how the corpus and the degree baseline's test numbers change compared to playground-only.
evals.expected_output: Runs schemaorg_fixtures.py then build_fixtures.py; reports ~143 total fixtures (train grows to ~125), a handful of schemaorg eval tasks, and compares degree test hits@1/MRR before/after.
assertions: schemaorg_fixtures.py and build_fixtures.py were both run
reports the merged fixture/split counts from the manifest
notes that subTypeOf edges are context-only (not masked) or that schema.org mainly enriches training
